name: Amazon River Dolphin
description: Amazon River Dolphins are famously known for their pink color, which comes from their diet, environmental conditions, and unique biological chracteristics.

name: Atlantic Spotted Dolphin
description: Calves are born unspotted and gradually develop their pattern over several years. This helps biologists estimate their age during identification. They're also known for cooperative hunting, sometimes working with bottlenose dolphins to corral fish.

name: Atlantic White-sided Dolphin
description: The Atlantic white-sided dolphin gets its name from the distinctive white stripe on its side, which starts just below the dorsal fin and runs into a yellow/ochre blaze continuing onto the tailstock.

name: Baiji
description: Also called the "Goddess of the Yangtze" in Chinese folklore, the baiji evolved in freshwater for roughly 20 million years, making it one of the oldest dolphin lineages. A 2006 expedition failed to find a single individual, leading scientists to declare it "functionally extinct" - the first cetacean extinction directly attributed to human activity.

name: Beaked Whale
description: This group includes 22+ poorly understood species, and Cuvier's Beaked Whale holds the record for the deepest and longest dive ever recorded in a marine mammal - nearly 3,000 meters and almost 3 hours and 42 minutes.

name: Beluga Whale
description: Belugas are one of the only whales with unfused cervical vertebrae, giving them a flexible neck that can turn independently of their body - a rarity among cetaceans. Their bulbous "melon" (forehead) can change shape as they vocalize

name: Bhulan
description: This Indus River dolphin subspecies is functionally blind and navigate entirely by echolocation in the murky rivers of Pakistan and India. It also swims on its side most of the time, which allows its head to sweep constantly from side to side for bottom-dwelling prey.

name: Blue Whale
description: The blue whale's heart alone can weigh as much as a small car, and its calls reach up to 188 decibles-that's louder than a jet engine! Calves drink up to 60 gallons of milk daily, allowing them to gain 4kg (9 lbs) every hour.

name: Bottlenose Dolphin
description: Each bottlenose dolphin develops a unique whistle in its first year of life that acts as an acoustic name-other dolphins use it to identify and call to specific individuals. They're also one of the few non-human animals confirmed to recognize themselves in mirrors which proves they possess a physical sense of self.
status: Least Concern (Critically Endangered: Fiordland, New Zealand)

name: Bottlenose Whale
description: Northern Bottlenose Whales are the largest members of the beaked whale family in the North Atlantic Ocean where they prefer cold, deep, temperate-sub-arctic oceanic waters. They're cryptic and skittish which makes it difficult-distinguish between them. Southern Bottlenose Whales are less studied and near threatened in IUCN status while Northern Bottlenose Whale are still prevalent.

name: Bowhead Whale
description: Bowheads may be the longest-lived mammals on Earth-some individuals have been found with 19th-century harpoon fragments embedded in their blubber, and eye-lens analysis suggests lifespans exceeding 200 years.

name: Bryde's Whale
description: Unlike most baleen whales, Bryde's whales don't undertake long seasonal migrations to polar feeding grounds-rather, theys stay in warm tropical waters year round. Their name is pronounced "broo-dus," after the Norwegian whaler it's named for.
status: Least Concern (Critically Endangered: Gulf of Mexico)

name: Burmeister's Porpoise
description: Unlike other cetaceans whose dorsal fins are triangular or sickle-shaped and sit near the middle of their back, the Burmeister's porpoise has a uniquely low, backward-pointing dorsal fin positioned well behind the center of its body. The leading edge is lined with small, hard bumps called tubercles.

name: Chilean Dolphin
description: Also known as the "black dolphin," this species is exclusive to the coast of Chile and thrives in cold, shallow waters. The 'black dolphin' name originated from early historical observations of stranded or dead specimens' skins appearing to darken to black when exposed to air.

name: Clymene Dolphin
description: Clymene dolphins evolved as a distinct species from the interbreeding of spinner dolphins and striped dolphins without changing its number of chromosomes. Its unique behavior, like the spinning jumps, is a behavioral link to its spinner dolphin ancestry.

name: Commerson's Dolphin
description: The commerson's dolphin, also referred to as the panda dolphin, are famous for being energetic, fast swimmers (up to 15 km/h or faster), frequently surfing waves and swimming upside down to hunt visually in shallow coastal waters.

name: Common Dolphin
description: Common dolphins form some of the largest social groups of any cetacean, with "superpods" numbering in the thousands to corral and herd massive schools of fish or squid. They're highly vocal and social, often mixing with other dolphin species and even pilot whales while foraging.

name: Dall's Porpoise
description: Dall's porpoise are the largest of the porpoise species and can swim up to 55 km per hour! Swimming this speed near the ocean's surface produces their iconic rooster tail of bursting sea spray. They're also one of the few animals that can out swim a killer whale.

name: Dusky Dolphin
description: Dusky dolphins are known for their high energy spinning leaps, backflips, and aerial displays.This helps synchronize pod movement in groups when herding schooling fish into tight balls near the surface.

name: Dwarf Sperm Whale
description: When startled or threatened, the whale expels a foul-smelling liquid, which can rapidly disperse and cloud an area of up to 100 square meters. The reddish hue can make the whale appear severely injured, confusing attackers and buying them time to escape.

name: False Killer Whale
description: False killer whales are large members of the oceanic dolphin family that earned their misleading name due to skull shapes resembling orcas (killer whales). They form tight, long-term social bonds and have been observed sharing food with humans and other dolphin species, a rare form of interspecies generosity. The main Hawaiian Islands insular false killer whale population is listed as endangered under the U.S. Endangered Species Act, with recent estimates numbering only about 139 individuals.

name: Fin Whale
description: Nicknamed the "greyhound of the sea," fin whales are the fastest of the large whales, capable of sustained speeds over 35 km/h. They also display unusual facial pigmentation asymmetry where the lower jaw is white on the right side and dark on the left.

name: Finless Porpoise
description: The finless porpoise is the only known porpoise species that completely lacks a dorsal fin, featuring instead a low, bumpy ridge of tubercles along its back. It inhabits shallow coastal and river waters across Asia, including a critically endangered population in China's Yangtze River.

name: Franciscana
description: This species has the longest beak in proportion to body size of any dolphin. Its long, slender snout can account for up to 15% of its total body length and is packed with over 200 teeth to snap up small fish, squid, and shrimp.

name: Fraser's Dolphin
description: The Fraser's dolphin is famous for being a "Lazarus species" originally believed to be extinct when an original skeleton was found washed up on a beach in Sarawak, Borneo, in 1895 by Charles Hose. It was sent to the British Museum, but wasn't formally described as a new species by scientist Francis Fraser until 1956. In 1971, live populations were finally rediscovered  in the tropical Pacific and the Atlantic.

name: Gray Whale
description: Gray whales complete one of the longest annual migrations of any mammal, traveling roughly 16,000 to 20,000 kilometers round-trip between Arctic feeding grounds and the protected lagoons of Baja California. As bottom feeders, they feed on amphipods and other invertebrates, scooping up sediment from the sea floor and filtering it through baleen plates, leaving behind distinct feeding pits and mud plumes.
status: Least Concern (Critically Endangered: Western North Pacific Population)

name: Harbor Porpoise
description: Harbour porpoises have sometimes been described as 'living in the fast lane.' Being smaller than other cetaceans and living in cold northern waters means that the porpoises require a lot of energy to survive, making them prone to starvation. Going without food for even a day or two can be life-threatening!
status: Least Concern (Critically Endangered: Baltic Sea Proper)

name: Hawaiian Monk Seal
description: The Hawaiian monk seal is the most endangered pinniped in U.S. waters and one of the most endangered seals worldwide. Most Hawaiian monk seals live in the remote Northwestern Hawaiian Islands where their numbers have declined since the 1950s.
status: Vulnerable (Endangered: US ESA listing, Northwestern Hawaiian Islands)

name: Heaviside's Dolphin
description: Heaviside's dolphin is found exclusively in the cold, coastal waters of the Benguela Current along the western coasts of South Africa and Namibia. Because its entire population is concentrated in this narrow geographic strip, the species is uniquely vulnerable to localized environmental pressures and human activities.

name: Hector's Dolphin
description: Hector's dolphins are the smallest and rarest marine dolphins in the world. They have distinct black facial markings, short stocky bodies, and a dorsal fin shaped like a Mickey Mouse ear. They are divided into two main groups: the South Island Hector's dolphin and the critically endangered Maui dolphin on the North Island's west coast.

name: Hourglass Dolphin
description: Named for the hourglass-shaped black-and-white pattern along its sides, this dolphin is one of the few cetaceans commonly seen in the frigid, remote waters of the Southern Ocean, often near Antarctic pack ice.

name: Humpback Dolphin
description: Humpback dolphins, known as Chinese or Hong Kong white dolphins are a variety of the Indo-Pacific humpbacked dolphins of South-East Asia and Australia. They are born black and gradually change colour to grey and white, but when they are in warm tropical waters their colling mechanism kicks in and passes blood through surface blood vessle, giving them a pink appearance.

name: Humpback Whale
description: Male humpback whales sing long, complex, and structured songs that last up to 30 minutes and spread across entire ocean populations like cultural music trends.

name: Irrawaddy Dolphin
description: In Myanmar, the Irrawaddy dolphin has learned to fish in a mutually beneficial way together with cast net fishermen, termed "cooperative fishing". Communication via calls and signals is made by both dolphins and fishermen, with the dolphins rearing schools of fish towards the cast net fishing boats and signalling to the fishermen to throw their nets when the fish near close to the boat.
status: Endangered (Critically Endangered: Mekong River, Mahakam River, Malampaya Sound)

name: Killer Whale
description: The killer whale, also known as orca, is the ocean's top predator. It is the largest member of the Delphinidae family, or dolphins.  They process emotions primarily through a highly specialized brain structure called the paralimbic lobe, which is an extra, highly folded lobe of tissue that humans and other land mammals entirely lack. This structure bridges the whale's analytical cerebral cortex with its limbic system (the core emotion-processing center in all mammals).
status: Data Deficient (Endangered: Southern Resident Population, Pacific Northwest)

name: Long-finned Pilot Whale
description: This species is one of only a handful of mammals, alongside humans, orcas, and a few other toothed whales, known to undergo menopause, with females living for decades after their reproductive years, likely to help care for grand-offspring.

name: Marine Debris
description: There are an estimated 5.25 trillion pieces of plastic debris floating in the world's oceans and scientists estimate by the year 2050, that ocean plastic will outweigh all of the fish in the sea.

name: Melon-headed Whale
description: Melon-headed whales often occur in groups of hundreds to over 1,000 animals. Smaller, coordinated subgroups are common within the larger groups. They are often associated with schools of Fraser's dolphins and have been sighted in mixed schools with other dolphins. They make fast, low leaps from the water as they swim and tends to rest in the morning, socialize in the afternoon, and forage at night on fish, squid, cuttlefish, and shrimp.

name: Minke Whale
description: Minke whales are the smallest members of the rorqual family but, despite their size, are remarkable ocean predators. When they surface to breathe, they often erupt quickly, exhaling a low, bushy blow that can look and sound like a sharp "sneeze." Unlike larger whales, they rarely raise their flukes out of the water when diving.

name: Narwhal
description: The narwhal's iconic tusk is actually an elongated left canine tooth that can grow up to 3 meters long, and it's packed with millions of nerve ending, helping the mammal detect subtle shifts in water temperature, pressure, and salinity. Male narwhals use the tusk for sparring, dominance, and social signaling.

name: Pacific White-sided Dolphin
description: The Pacific white-sided dolphin is well-known for its vibrant energy, intelligence, and highly social behavior. They have a tendency to leap, flip, and interact with ships by bowriding. They frequently associate with Northern right whale dolphins, Risso's dolphins, and short-finned pilot whales, even swimming alongside giant baleen whales like humpbacks.

name: Peale's Dolphin
description: Peale's dolphin, also known as the black-chinned dolphin, is a small cetacean native entirely to the cold, coastal waters of southern South America. They are often referred to as "dolphins of the kelp" due to their tight ecological relationship with giant kelp beds and often use a "starburst" or encircling formation to trap bottom-dwelling fish, octopuses, squid, and crustaceans within or near the kelp.

name: Pygmy Killer Whale
description: Pygmy killer whales are among the most elusive marine mammals and are highly avoidant of watercraft, preferring deep tropical and subtropical open oceans. In the wild, they are generally cooperative, social, and form strong, lifelong social bonds within pods of up to 50 individuals. Because their pods exhibit intense loyalty and tightly pack together when threatened or alarmed, a single sick or disoriented leader can lead an entire pod onto a beach stranding. However, when placed in captivity, they have historically exhibited extreme aggression and experience lower survival rates.

name: Pygmy Right Whale
description: The smallest and least understood of all baleen whales, this species is known almost entirely from strandings-live sightings at sea are exceptionally rare, and its social behavior and migration patterns remain largely a mystery.

name: Pygmy Sperm Whale
description: Like its dwarf relative, this species can release a cloud of dark intestinal fluid when threatened, functioning as a "smokescreen" to help it escape predators like sharks.

name: Right Whale
description: Right whales are identified by researchers using the unique pattern of rough, callused skin patches on their heads, which function like a fingerprint. Their name comes from whalers who considered them the "right" whale to hunt-they were slow, floated after death, and yielded abundant oil and baleen.
status: Least Concern (Critically Endangered: North Atlantic & North Pacific Populations)

name: Right Whale Dolphin
description: This is the only dolphin species with no dorsal fin whatsoever, giving it a streamlined, torpedo-like profile thought to reduce drag for fast, sustained swimming in open ocean environments.

name: Risso's Dolphin
description: Risso's dolphins are born dark gray or brown and accumulate extensive white linear scars over time from interactions with prey and other dolphins, causing older adults to appear almost completely white.

name: Rough-toothed Dolphin
description: Rough-toothed dolphins are highly intelligent, highly sociable marine mammals known for traveling in tight, synchronized groups and exhibiting strong empathetic care behaviors.  They have a small head and are the only long-beaked dolphins without a noticeable crease between their beak and forehead.

name: Sei Whale
description: Sei whales are fast, solitary swimmers that dive by quietly sinking below the surface rather than arching their backs. They are usually observed alone or in small groups of two to five animals, though larger numbers can gather where food is abundant.

name: Short-finned Pilot Whale
description: Short-finned pilot whales are highly social, deep-diving marine mammals known for their tight-knit matrilineal pods and high-speed hunting dashes. Females stay in their birth pod for life, while males often move between groups. They are frequently observed "logging", where they rest motionless at the surface, often in the morning after a night of active foraging and exhibit behaviors like spy-hopping (popping their heads straight up to look around) and fluke or tail slapping, which older males may use defensively or aggressively when boats approach.

name: Spectacled Porpoise
description: Spectacled porpoises are elusive and quiet marine mammals known for moving in unobtrusive, small groups of 1 to 5 individuals. Unlike many dolphins, they rarely leap or perform acrobatic displays at the surface and tend to avoid approaching vessels, though some have shown fast swimming behaviors when boats get close.

name: Sperm Whale
description: Sperm whales are the largest toothed predators on Earth, famous for their massive heads and record-breaking deep dives. Their large square heads account for about one-third of their total body length and they possess the largest brain of any animal on Earth, weighing up to 20 pounds (9 kg)! They are also the only cetacean with an asymmetrical blowhole, with a single blowhole placed on the left side of the head.

name: Spinner Dolphin
description: Spinner dolphins are small, highly acrobatic marine mammals famous for leaping up to 10 feet into the air and spinning around their body axis up to seven times in a single jump.

name: Spotted Dolphin
description: The pantropical spotted dolphin is slender and highly social. Found in tropical and subtropical waters worldwide, they have a long, thin beak, a distinct white tip on the mouth, and the thinnest dorsal fin of any dolphin species.Calves are born completely unspotted and distinctive white and dark spots develop and increase in number and size as they age.

name: Striped Dolphin
description: Striped dolphins feature a bluish-grey back, light grey flanks, and a white or pinkish belly, accented by bold dark stripes running from their eyes toward their flippers and tail. Their diet primarily consists of small mid-water or deep-water fish and they form tight, active pods usually numbering between 25 and 100 individuals, though larger groups can reach the hundreds of thousands. Known for exceptional speed and leaps, they perform a unique maneuver called roto-tailing, where they leap high and vigorously rotate their tails while airborne.

name: Susu
description: The susu is a rare freshwater dolphin native to the murky rivers of South Asia. It gets its popular name from the distinctive whistling or blowing sound it makes when it comes up to breathe. They are functionally blind because their eyes lack lenses and have flat corneas, meaning they cannot form clear images. This means they rely entirely on echolocation to hunt and move through muddy waters. They also possess unusually flexible neck vertebrae that let them turn their heads up to 90 degrees.

name: Tiger Shark
description: Tiger sharks are named for the dark spots and vertical bars running down their bodies, which are prominent in juveniles and fade as adults. They possess uniquely serrated, sideways-pointing teeth with deep notches designed to slice through tough prey like turtle shells and bone and are known as the "garbage cans of the sea," due to their indiscriminate diet which includes inedible man-made debris like car license plates, tires, and cans.

name: Tucuxi
description: The Tucuxi is a small freshwater dolphin found in the rivers and floodplains of the Amazon and Orinoco basins. Together, they are extremely sociable and execute impressive stunts such as spyhopping, lobtailing, flipper-slapping and porpoising. They are, however, not keen on socialising with people and prefer to keep to themselves. When they dive, tucuxi tend to only stay down for short periods of time, usually lasting 30 seconds to one minute.

name: Vaquita
description: The vaquita is the world's smallest living cetacean and the world's most endangered marine mammal-found only in a tiny part of the Gulf of California.

name: Whale Shark
description: The whale shark is the largest living fish in the world, recognizable by its massive size, broad flat head, and unique checkerboard pattern of white spots and stripes. They have extremely thick skin that can measure up to 4 inches (10 cm) or more on the back and mainly consume plankton, krill, fish eggs, small squid, and small schooling fish like sardines and anchovies by straining water through specialized gill plates.

name: White-beaked Dolphin
description: White-beaked dolphins are found throughout the cold waters of the North Atlantic Ocean. They are active swimmers and often surf the waves created by vessels. They are usually found in groups of five to 30 individuals but sometimes travel in groups of up to 1,500. Some fishermen in Canada call these dolphins "squidhounds" because they eat squid and octopi.
